note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one City of Albuquerque page - the pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court Locations" table gives every venue a name, an address and a description cell that states the kind of court and the count, and whose prose beneath the table states hours for the two complexes, the first come, first served rule with its ninety-minute limit, the Sierra Vista phone reservation and the lesson programme - plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. The City writes most addresses without a street type and the Census supplied one; every published address matched at house-number level without a second resolver. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Thirty-three pickleball courts, twenty-one of them lit, at the City of Albuquerque's principal pickleball complex in the south-east of the city. The City's table cell reads "Pickleball Complex / 33 Courts (21 Lighted)", and its prose names this as the first of the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes", so these are pickleball courts rather than tennis courts carrying a second set of lines.

Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex's thirty-three is the largest single-venue count on this site; Mesa's Tennis & Pickleball Center, at twenty-one, held that place before this run. The number is new to the record in two senses. The imported dataset carried this venue at eighteen courts, and the City's page source still holds "18 Courts (6 Lighted)" inside a comment no browser renders; the visible table says thirty-three, the visible table is what publishes, and the venue is marked for a re-check at the next cadence because the count changed.

This is also where the City teaches the game. Its 2026 lessons - Junior Basics, Adult Basics and Intermediate Play - "will take place at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex", with classes "limited to six participants" and registration online at play.cabq.gov or through staff at the Jerry Cline Tennis Facility, 505-224-6682.

The City writes the address without a street type, as it does nearly everywhere in its table, and the US Census address geocoder matched it as "501 ELIZABETH ST SE" at house-number level, in Bernalillo County and inside the incorporated place Albuquerque. The City's quadrant, SE, is carried through unchanged; the postcode is the resolver's, since the City's visible table prints none. Lauren C. Bolles, with eight lined courts, publishes in the same postcode.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the complex and nothing about restrooms. What it does publish is two phone numbers: the reservations line for the whole programme, 505-224-6682, and the City Pickleball Manager, 505-224-6693.
slots.what_to_expect:
Open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, in the City's sentence "Manzano Mesa, Villella, and Pat Hurley are open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily." With twenty-one lit courts, the evening end of that window is usable, which is the case at no other published venue in Albuquerque; the other twelve courts here carry no lighting statement, so after dark the complex is a twenty-one-court complex on the City's record.

Play is "on a first come, first serve basis" and "limited to 1.5 hours when others are waiting" - a ninety-minute cap that presumes a queue, and thirty-three courts is a scale at which turning up alone and finding a game is a reasonable plan even though the City publishes no open-play time. The complex can be reserved for special events and tournaments through the City's Sports Office, so a tournament day is a day the courts may be taken; lessons run here on summer weekday mornings at 8, 9 and 10 a.m. and on spring and autumn Saturdays. Price, surface, nets and indoor or outdoor are not stated.

This site publishes the table's spelling, Villela, and notes the other.

A dedicated court is a pickleball court whenever you arrive, with nothing to share and nothing to set up. In Albuquerque that puts Villela in a group of two with Manzano Mesa, against nine parks where the count is a count of lines on tennis courts. Six courts is enough for a rotation rather than a single game, and it is the same six as Montgomery Park's lined set and Sierra Vista's two-plus-four, but with all six standing as pickleball courts all day.

The venue was in the imported dataset before the City's page was read, as "Villela Park Pickleball Courts" with a longer address and no set schedule; the City's table overrode the name and the address, the City's prose supplied the hours, and the count of six was confirmed.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts of two kinds at a City tennis complex in the north-west, and the six is the City's own arithmetic. The table reads "Tennis/Pickleball Courts / 2 Courts and 4 Lined Courts", and the prose says the same thing in longer words: one of "two shared complexes at Sierra Vista Courts with 2 permanent pickleball courts, and 4 lined pickleball courts". Two courts stand as pickleball courts; four are lines on tennis courts. Both figures are printed here so the sum can be checked, and the distinction matters on arrival, because two of the six are certain and four depend on what the tennis courts are being used for.

This is the one Albuquerque venue whose courts the City says can be booked: "Courts at Sierra Vista can be reserved in advanced by calling 505-767-5445." That number is the complex's own, distinct from the Sports Office reservations line for tournaments and special events. The City states no price for a reservation, and a phone booking with no stated cost is not read here as a fee.

The other "shared complex" the City names, Pat Hurley Park, is refused on its address, so Sierra Vista is the only venue of its kind that publishes in Albuquerque. It has no imported row and is minted from the City's table.

Without a booking the rule is the City's general one - "first come, first serve", ninety minutes when others are waiting - and with a booking, made by phone, a court is yours for the time agreed at a price the City does not state.

Hours are not stated: the City's 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. sentence names Manzano Mesa, Villella and Pat Hurley and not Sierra Vista. Lighting is not stated. For a player who wants certainty, the phone number is the whole point of this venue - it is the one place in Albuquerque where the City says a court can be secured rather than queued for, and the two permanent courts are the ones worth securing.
